recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV latest (44.0 ms) is 31% below baseline (63.9 ms) — a clinically meaningful suppression
Sleep avg 4.6h/night (15/14 days <7h) — severe chronic sleep debt
Training readiness score is 26 (scale 0–100), well below functional threshold (~60+)
Recovery balance is 1.61, but this reflects low load — not strong recovery (HRV z-score is likely negative; load z-score is strongly negative due to acute load of 159 vs chronic 229)
ACWR = 0.6 — far below safe range (0.8–1.3), indicating significant detraining pressure, not restful recovery
readiness.guidance: This is not recovered fatigue — it's systemic under-recovery with sleep deficit and autonomic suppression; the priority is restoring sleep and nervous system resilience before adding any training stress.

monthly_review.summary: August shows sharply reduced volume and intensity versus July, with pace improving slightly but at the cost of dramatically lower cadence and aerobic TE, suggesting compromised neuromuscular function and fatigue masking true fitness gains.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +35 spm (118 → 153) — an outlier shift inconsistent with prior months (June: 151, May: 146, April: 142) and likely driven by very short, high-cadence efforts (e.g., 0.5 km @ 153 spm on 8/8 and 4.5 km @ 159 spm on 8/13), not sustainable aerobic development.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 55.3 km across 8 sessions in 17 days — ~3.25 km/session, 3x/week minimum. Given severely compromised readiness (HRV down 31%, sleep avg 4.6h, readiness score 26), chasing this volume is medically inadvisable and risks injury or burnout; recovery, not volume, is the priority.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated Running Economy
insights.body: Sleep avg 4.6h (vs baseline 4.5h) coincides with latest Running Economy at 253.5 ml O2/kg/km — the highest in recent record and rated 'Recreational' (worse); poor sleep impairs mitochondrial efficiency and neuromuscular coordination, increasing oxygen cost per km.

insights.title: Low ACWR (0.6) masks autonomic fatigue, not freshness
insights.body: ACWR is low due to acute load dropping to 159 (chronic 229), but HRV latest is 44.0 ms — 31% below baseline — and resting HR dropped only modestly (-1.0 bpm), confirming parasympathetic withdrawal rather than recovery; low load here reflects inability to train, not readiness.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling improved (4.8%) despite poor sleep and low volume
insights.body: Latest decoupling is 4.8% — within ideal <5% band — suggesting preserved aerobic endurance integrity, even as other metrics (cadence volatility, efficiency decline) point to neuromuscular fatigue; this highlights dissociation between central (cardiovascular) and peripheral (muscular/coordination) fatigue.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance (43%) without Z5 work reduces per-beat efficiency
insights.body: Z3 accounts for 43% of August volume (vs 29% in July), yet efficiency per HR beat in Z3 (0.7516 m/beat) is lower than Z2 (0.7901 m/beat); overreliance on Z3 without Z5 stimulus may reflect ‘no-man’s land’ training that stresses systems without driving adaptation.

recommendations.action: Prioritize 7+ hours of sleep for 5 consecutive nights — no exceptions, no catch-up naps; use body battery trend (currently 63.1, down 2.8% vs baseline) as feedback
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is the primary driver of HRV suppression and impaired Running Economy

recommendations.action: One 30-min Zone 1 walk or mobility session (HR <115 bpm) on Tuesday and Friday, zero running
recommendations.reason: To stimulate vagal tone without cardiovascular or musculoskeletal load; current recovery balance (1.61) and readiness score (26) contraindicate any running

recommendations.action: Skip all structured runs until resting HR stabilizes ≥51 bpm AND HRV recovers to ≥58 ms for 3 consecutive days
recommendations.reason: Resting HR remains suppressed (50.4 bpm, down from 51.4) and HRV is critically low (44.0 ms); resuming running prematurely will entrench autonomic dysregulation

risk_flags.evidence: HRV latest = 44.0 ms (31% below baseline 63.9 ms); resting HR suppressed (50.4 bpm); training readiness = 26
risk_flags.action: Immediate sleep prioritization and zero running for ≥5 days

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence spiked erratically (118 → 153 spm) while vertical oscillation rose to 8.0% (vs 5.5–6.6% in July), indicating inefficient, high-impact stride likely due to fatigue
risk_flags.action: Suspend all running until vertical oscillillation stabilizes ≤7.0% and cadence normalizes to 146–151 spm range

risk_flags.risk: Metabolic inefficiency from chronic sleep loss
risk_flags.evidence: Running Economy worsened to 253.5 ml O2/kg/km (‘Recreational’ rating) while sleep avg = 4.6h and 15/14 days <7h
risk_flags.action: Target 7+ h sleep nightly for 10 days before reassessing economy trends

weekly_focus.description: This week is not about running — it’s about reversing autonomic fatigue and rebuilding sleep architecture to restore HRV, normalize gait efficiency, and re-establish metabolic resilience.
suggested_sessions: 15-min guided diaphragmatic breathing + HRV biofeedback (target: HRV >55 ms)
Mobility routine focused on hip flexor release and plantar fascia gliding (no loading)
